name: Botswana
system_note: The president is elected by parliament and heads the government.
snapshot: One of Africa's most stable democracies, now led by its first opposition government and searching for a future beyond diamonds as global demand slumps.
culture: Botswana takes its name from the Tswana people, and Setswana is spoken by nearly everyone alongside English. The kgotla, a village assembly where elders and residents debate in public, is a living tradition that the state still uses for consultation. Cattle remain central to status and family wealth. The Okavango Delta and the Kalahari underpin a high-end safari industry that deliberately limits visitor numbers.
society: At independence in 1966 Botswana was among the poorest countries on Earth; diamond revenue, managed through a joint venture with De Beers, built roads, schools and clinics. The country fought one of the world's worst HIV epidemics and now has high treatment coverage. Unemployment, especially among young people, is stubbornly high, and the slump in natural diamond prices has hit state finances hard.
baseline: In October 2024 voters ended 58 years of rule by the Botswana Democratic Party, which fell to fourth place. Duma Boko, a Harvard-trained lawyer leading the Umbrella for Democratic Change, became president. His government inherited a recession driven by collapsing diamond sales as lab-grown stones undercut the market, and has sought a bigger stake in the De Beers partnership and new investment in other sectors.
